summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly (Bash + Read + one Edit to index.html) within ~15s, with no clarifying questions and no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: The request was handled as a mechanical edit: a single Edit tool call added `<input type=\"checkbox\"> Done` to index.html, confirmed by grep of the file. No Skill tool call of any kind appears in the session JSONL, so brainstorming was not invoked. Both acceptance criteria pass.

observations.description: coding-agent-token-usage.json (the headline cost artifact named by the scenario) does not exist in the results directory; `ls` shows only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json. It may be written post-run, but I could not verify the token total.
Launch required four separate confirmation dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before the prompt was usable, despite the run being pre-seeded with dialog-bypass state.
Agent's final message said "Not committed; no tests exist in this repo to run" — clear and appropriately scoped for a trivial edit.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Read 1 file, ran 1 shell command" then Update(index.html) adding `<input type="checkbox"> Done`, finishing with "Brewed for 15s". Session log tool sequence: thinking→Bash→Read→thinking→Edit→text, no questions back to user.

`grep -o '"name":"Skill"' home/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` returned nothing (exit 1); the only 'brainstorming' hits (3 lines) are system-prompt/skill-catalog text, e.g. "names":["hyperpowers:brainstorming",...] in the initial skillCount:27 listing.
